literature_notes: All five ledger lines (L1–L5) describe C-terminal fusions or tags on full-length JAG1. L1 reports a JAG1-APEX2 (with embedded FLAG) C-terminal fusion; L2–L3 report a JAG1-eGFP C-terminal fusion used for live imaging; L4–L5 report a C-terminal HA-tagged JAG1 (JAG1-HA) used for co-immunoprecipitation. JAG1 is a type I single-pass transmembrane protein: the ectodomain spans residues 34–1068, the TM helix 1069–1089, and the intracellular tail 1090–1218. All cited tags are therefore appended to the intracellular C-terminus (after V1218) and face the cytoplasm, not the extracellular space. No ledger line describes any tag insertion at the extracellular N-terminus (after the signal peptide cleavage at residue 33), in any extracellular loop, or at any internal extracellular junction. Because no ledger evidence supports an extracellular surface tag on JAG1, zero sites are proposed.

literature_other_positions.note: JAG1-APEX2 (with FLAG) and JAG1-eGFP are C-terminal fusions appended after the last residue (V1218), which lies in the intracellular tail (residues 1090–1218); the tag faces the cytoplasm, not the extracellular surface.
JAG1-HA is explicitly described as a C-terminal HA-tagged construct; the C-terminus (V1218) is intracellular, so the HA tag is cytoplasmic and not accessible on the cell surface.
